basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 28.' and it opens 'Vers. 28. Mortuus est Aran et Thare in Ur Chaldaeorum. Tradunt Hebraei quod Abraham et'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 28. Mortuus est Aran et Thare in Ur Chaldaeorum. Tradunt Hebraei quod Abraham et Aran fratres, cum nollent ignem adorare, in ignem projecti sunt ex quo miserante Deo Abraham illaesus exivit. Unde et saepe Deus ad illum dicit: Ego sum Deus qui te eripui de Ur Chaldaeorum. Aran vero igne consumptus est. Ergo Ur non est nomen loci.
